title: GRACE IN THE LINE OF THE KING

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When the time came for her to give birth, there were twin boys in her womb. As she was giving birth, one of them put out his hand; so the midwife took a scarlet thread and tied it on his wrist and said, 'This one came out first.' But when he drew back his hand, his brother came out, and she said, 'So this is how you have broken out!' And he was named Perez. Then he broke out, his brother came out with the scarlet thread on his wrist, and he was named Zerah." - Gen 38:27-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter ends with the birth of twins to Tamar — a surprising, even chaotic delivery, in which the second baby "breaks out" ahead of the one whose hand appeared first. He is named Perez, meaning "breaking out." After all the sin, injustice, and heartache of this chapter, it closes with new life.

But the true wonder of these babies is not revealed until much later. Perez, born from this tangled and sinful story, becomes an ancestor of King David — and through David, of Jesus Christ Himself (Ruth 4:18-22; Matt 1:3). And remarkably, when Matthew lists Jesus' family tree, he names Tamar, the wronged and desperate widow, right there in the Messiah's line (Matt 1:3).

Think of the grace in this. God took one of the most sordid, broken episodes in Genesis — full of sin, deception, and injustice — and wove it into the very lineage of the Saviour of the world. He did not wait for a clean, respectable story; He worked His redemption right through the mess.

This is the gospel in miniature. God's grace is not reserved for the polished and the proper. He delights to bring His salvation through broken people and shameful situations, redeeming what looks beyond repair. Whatever mess is in your story or your family's past, take heart: the God who brought the King's line through Judah and Tamar can weave His grace through your story too.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I believe God can bring grace through broken and shameful situations?
2. How does God's redemption of this story give me hope for my own?
3. Where do I need to trust God to weave good through a mess?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You wove Your grace through even this broken story, bringing the line of Christ through it. Give me hope that You can redeem the messes in my own story too. Amen.
